title: A Score of Time
subtitle: Notes come together and dance, unaware they are about to become a complete song.

trails.title: An Unexpected Encounter
trails.description: An accident occurred here once, but fortunately, no one was hurt.

content.text:
Surrounded by light but feeling no pain. The screams and footsteps around her are crystal clear.

The first footsteps she hears are Kozlov and Natalya's. Their voices are more familiar than her own heartbeat.

The clatter of goat hooves belongs to Elijah, still midway through his riding performance.

The particularly light, quick footsteps are Fracios's, a habit left from his juggling practice.

"Everyone stay calm. Her Arcanum has protected her very well." A strange voice. Must be an audience member stepping onto the stage. "Relax, girl. Try not to think too much. Just tell me, what you see right now?"

"This is unbelievable. I see a star, a shooting star is flying right toward me."

The stranger crouches beside her. The light dims just a little. "I'm going to use Ley Lines to dissolve your Arcanum. Stay relaxed. Talk to me about anything. What hobbies do you have?"

"Maybe they're not really hobbies, but ... I like to listen to the radio and weather reports. I also like exploring strange places. To keep from getting lost, I memorize all the unusual-looking trees and rocks along the way ... That star is still twinkling. That's not normal, right?"

"Don't worry. Maybe everything today happened just so you could meet that star. Let's keep talking. Would you like to study Ley Lines with me? You have a real talent, I'm sure of it ..."

trails.title: The Great Utrennyaya Circus
trails.description: Darkness all around. What an unforgettable experience.

content.text:
We have the best stage on Earth, each show as unique as a flake of snow.

We bring the most spirited performances in the world.

Elijah can turn any animal into the finest steed alive.

Fracios's performances will make you laugh until you cry.

And Kiperina, our tiny and adorable aerialist, walks on a wire so thin no one can even see it.

Ringmaster Kozlov has folded his entire life's reputation into this little tent.

From now until next month, this new world welcomes you!

items.speaker: Radio
items.text: "We believe Voyager 1 will continue to explore the galaxy on and on ..."

items.speaker: Radio
items.text: "Traveling into the depths of the universe, carrying with it humanity's spirit of exploration, it is likely to persist longer than life on Earth ..."
The radio catches her new friend's attention in an odd way. She's spent the past few days fascinated with the little musical box.
Until another voice cuts through the broadcast.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: What will the weather be like tomorrow? Maybe we can take a longer walk if it's sunny.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: You haven't seen the diamond mine here in Mirny, have you?
The girl shakes her head, sets the radio aside, and waits for Kiperina to speak.
Kiperina kneels down. Now, they're eye to eye.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: Is anything coming back to you? I asked some people around about you, but no one had any clue.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: Don't worry. Most of us in the circus were adopted by Mr. Kozlov, so he won't mind if you stay with us. He always gives a hand to those in need.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: And I'm going to meet an extraordinary lady tomorrow. She knows a lot. Maybe she will know who you are.

Kiperina is used to this kind of blank stare. She's seen it on the faces of children that were lost while they were at the circus—how Mrs. Kozlov had comforted them, and kept them entertained until the smiles returned to their faces.
She stands up, steps back, and reaches her hand toward the girl.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: Hey, look at this.
A soft glow blooms at her fingertip, warming the tent with its light.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: It's my arcane skill. It's not very useful, I know, but don't you think it's pretty?

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: People say it looks like the stars.
... Mhm.
The tiny light served its purpose. She seems far more at ease now.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: I could do it again if you like.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: Let's try something. Can you spell your name?
The girl eyes the colorful, crooked row of blocks placed in front of her. She doesn't know anything about the writing of this planet, so there's no way to share her name or where she's from.
But this creature wants a name to communicate with her. She understands that much.
The blocks form a messy, colorful path. A logic forms in her mind.
Kiperina searches for something familiar among the colors.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: Long journey ... traveler?

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: *sigh* Sounds like you just picked these words up from the radio.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: Did you go on a long journey to reach Mirny?

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: Hmm. How was it that Mr. Kozlov decided on our stage names? Give me a second.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: "Long journey," we could call that a "voyage." That would make you, who traveled a long journey, a ...

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: Voyager.
Kiperina stretches out her hand and traces the imagined path of the Voyager probe.
The girl watches for a moment, then imitates the gesture.

items.speaker: Voyager
items.text: Kiperina.
She twists her finger and points to herself.

items.speaker: Voyager
items.text: Voyager.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: Now that you have a stage name, you are now an official member of the Utrennyaya Circus.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: Hmm?
Voyager spins herself toward the tent's entrance. A moment later, footsteps and a familiar, friendly voice arrive together.

items.speaker: Natalya Kozlov
items.text: Alia, where's that girl? The one who was staring at the animals before? I brought a bunny around for her.

items.speaker: Natalya Kozlov
items.text: I suppose I'll be looking after her now, because you're meeting those Laplace people tomorrow, right?

items.speaker: Natalya Kozlov
items.text: You need a rest, Alia. Now do as Mama Kozlov says: go have a nice meal at the restaurant in town and then straight to bed early.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: Mrs. Kozlov, I don't need to ...

items.speaker: Natalya Kozlov
items.text: Hush, just go. I didn't cook anything for you tonight. We've already paid the restaurant.
Voyager's head twists, unsure of where to look between the door and her new friend, but in the end, she chooses the fuzzy rabbit.
The tent falls quiet again, leaving Kiperina alone, looking helpless.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: I'm not just a little kid that you need to take care of.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: Fine. I'll go, and after that, I will train for another hour.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: Yes, that's for the best.
Restaurant, Town

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: That's all. Thanks.
She closes the menu and slides it across the counter.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Sorry, it sometimes takes us a while to decide on an order. So, you were saying you found a strange girl here in Mirny, and then?

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Hold on! That special device you're holding. Did you get it from Windsong?

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: Yes. Before I came to Mirny, I fell from the wire during a show, and Ms. Windsong happened to be there.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: I don't remember the details, but she said my arcane skill was able to protect me.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: She helped me draw out the aura from around my body and analyzed how it worked. Though I didn't understand that part at all.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: But the name of her theory is still clear in my mind—The Study of Ley Lines. She gave me this device before she left. She said it would make it easier to control my arcane skill.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: Mr. Kozlov wants me to give it a try again, so I've decided to go see her tomorrow.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Cool. She's a great researcher. The Study of Ley Lines is still highly theoretical, but as we say at Laplace, theory often lays the foundation for practice.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: If you do decide to join us, I'd be happy to write a reference letter for you.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: You're a Laplace researcher?

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: You didn't already guess? Hmm. My colleagues often say I dress, you know, like a mad scientist.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: I guess it's that I never thought I would meet a scientist eating at a little restaurant like this.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Oh, please, I'm sure you're aware that scientists are living things too. We need to eat just like everyone else.
A few little snakes poke out of Hissabeth's hair, nodding along with her laughter.
One tilts its head up, letting Kiperina stroke it. Its scales feel smooth and cold.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Looks like you meant it when you said you're good with animals.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: I spend a lot of time with them in the circus. I even helped raise one of our bear cubs.
Kiperina hadn't been in the restaurant long before Hissabeth walked in and sat right beside her.
One of the snakes takes the lead in inspecting Kiperina, who greets it kindly in return.
That's all it takes for the two to find common ground.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: You know you haven't answered my question yet. Why do you choose to be an acrobat?

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Don't you find it scary to walk on a wire all the way up in the air? I suppose it is a really cool job, though.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: Well, it is cool, I have to admit. But what I really like about being up on the wire is that, when you look down, you get to see a view that no one else gets to in their daily life.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: When I stand on the wire, the audience below look just like stars, and it feels like I'm floating in space with them.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: Isn't that great? In that moment, I stop worrying about my performance and forget all expectations. I can just be in the moment, shining like a star.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Oh, intriguing. You know, in a way, I came all the way out here because I had the same thought.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: I wanna work with the smartest minds in the world, whether humans or arcanists. They're also like the stars in a lot of ways, each one bound to go down in history.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: And I'm trying to find out what really exists beyond the limits of the sky.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: Do all your siblings share the same feeling? They're such neat little snakes. Oh, it looks like they have fallen asleep.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: We've always been on the same page when it comes to these things.
Hissabeth turns her head. Kiperina notices her pupils narrowing to a slit.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Your arcane skill is exactly as I expected.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: It captures photons from the aurora and stores them as latent energy; then, when it's deployed, it appears to form a kind of prismatic plasma barrier.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: Wh-What?

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: I'll explain next time. It's complicated. It could take hours to get it into your head.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Still, it is most obvious to me that you are exactly the person we want for this opportunity. What do you say? Will you give it a try?

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: An opportunity to reach the stars.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: You mean you're the colleague Ms. Windsong mentioned? The one who invited me to Mirny?

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: I should've known. Was this a test? I thought you were a friend I could talk to.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: A "friend"? Superbe, that's the best compliment I've received in months.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Relax, this wasn't a test at all. We just happen to share the same taste in food.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: But I do hope you'll consider our offer seriously, in the spirit of the good time we had together.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: Are you serious though? You really mean you want me to become an astronaut?
The invitation seems too far-fetched. Even in her wildest dreams, she could never have imagined it.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Exactly.
But Hissabeth's response carries a rare weight, different from her usual casual tone.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Don't rush to a decision. We can wait till tomorrow.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: In fact, the materials I've been expecting should arrive tomorrow as well. Maybe the delivery guy will bring you a small gift along the way.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: You don't have to. Sorry, I didn't prepare any gifts.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Don't be silly. It's just a friendly gesture. I believe you come from the same region, so I'll bet you two will get along quite famously. And he has an interesting nickname too. It was, umm, oh, right—
Name Day.
